To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Taspase processing affects TFIIAs regulation of TFIId and suggest that TFIId is required to establish selective core promoter activity in response to NC2.
Taspase 1 processing of TF II A alters TF II A cofactor properties in regulating TFIID.
Taspase 1 processing alters TFIA interactions with TFIId and the conformation and function of TFIId/TFIA promoter complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of TFIIA cofactors in the regulation of the transcription factor TFIID and how this regulation is altered by Taspase1 protease activity.
the role of Taspase1-mediated processing of the TFIIA cofactors in the regulation of the basal RNA transcription machinery.
the regulation of the basal transcription machinery and the mechanisms that ensure specific gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Taspase-1 processing of TFIIIα/β alters its cofactor properties in regulation of TFIIB.
Taspase-1 processing of TFIIIa alters TFIIIa cofactor properties in regulation of TFIIIa.
Taspase 1 processing affects TF II A interactions with TFI ID and the conformation TFI ID/TFIIA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TFIIA processing by Taspase1 alters TFIIA regulation in the TFIIB/TFIID/NC2 complex.
Taspase 1 processing of TFIA affects the ability to regulate TFIID and that this regulation is dependent on the INR.
Taspase processing of TFIIAs is required to establish a specific INR-selective transcriptional response in the presence of the repressor NC-2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Taspase-1 processing of TF II-A alters the properties of the TF II-A cofactor in the regulation of TF II-D.
TFIIA cofactors are not static, but can be modified in a proteolytic manner to regulate their function.
Taspase processing of TFIIAs is required to establish specific core promoter activity of TFIID.
